articles.headline: Running HIIT Triggers Bigger Immune Spike Than Cycling HIIT
articles.body: New research shows different HIIT workouts affect your immune system differently. When researchers compared running and cycling interval training, running HIIT produced a more inflammatory immune response. Both forms increased the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-6 during exercise and IL-10 after 24 hours. The findings matter because they help you choose workouts that deliver anti-inflammatory benefits while limiting excess tissue damage. If you're balancing hard training with recovery, knowing your workout choice matters.
articles.takeaway: Running HIIT creates a larger inflammatory response than cycling HIIT. Choose based on your recovery capacity that week.

articles.headline: Estrogen-Only Therapy Linked to Lower Alzheimer's Risk in Women
articles.body: A Stanford study of over 21,000 women found that those using estrogen-only menopausal hormone therapy had 39% lower odds of developing dementia compared to non-users. Researchers examined Alzheimer's pathology in autopsied brains and found hormone therapy users showed 35% lower odds of Alzheimer's markers. The findings challenge earlier fears about hormone therapy and suggest the right approach at the right time can protect cognitive health. This aligns with updated FDA guidance that removed black box warnings from hormone therapy products in 2026.
articles.takeaway: Estrogen-only therapy was associated with significantly lower dementia risk in this large study. Timing and individual factors matter—discuss with your doctor.

articles.headline: Nearly Half of Americans Now Meet CVD Criteria. The New Framework Changes Everything
articles.body: The 2026 American Heart Association statistics reveal a major shift in how doctors view heart disease. Instead of looking at isolated issues like high blood pressure or high cholesterol, clinicians now assess cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome—a framework that examines how your heart, kidneys, and metabolism work together. Fewer than 11% of American adults meet criteria for optimal CKM health, while 15% have advanced multisystem disease. This systems-level approach explains why some people with normal cholesterol still develop heart problems, and why prevention now focuses on the complete picture.
articles.takeaway: Your heart, kidneys, and metabolism are connected. Modern prevention looks at all three together, not individual numbers in isolation.

articles.topic: AI-powered wearables detect illness early warning signs
articles.headline: Your Wearable Is Now Predicting Health Crises Days Before You Feel Them
articles.body: The wearables industry has shifted from fitness tracking to clinical intelligence. In 2026, smartwatches and smart rings can now detect irregular heart rhythms, estimate blood glucose, and flag mental health crises a week before symptoms appear. The breakthrough is AI—the same device that tracked steps in 2020 now analyzes patterns from multiple sensors to predict illness and feed data directly into your doctor's records. FDA clearances for wearables are surging, and remote monitoring programs are expanding. The challenge isn't capability anymore; it's integration with healthcare systems and data privacy.
articles.takeaway: AI algorithms analyzing your wearable data can predict problems earlier than you notice symptoms. Accuracy continues to improve.
articles.source: Digital Health and Wearable Technology Analysis

workout.title: Twist & Release: Gentle Spinal Mobility & Breath Reset
workout.tip: Initiate all twists from your ribcage, not your lumbar spine. Lengthen your torso on the inhale, then gently deepen the twist on the exhale. This protects your lower back and ensures spinal rotation comes from the safest zone.
workout.warmup: 4 min: 5 gentle spinal rolls supine, 10 dead bugs, 5 windshield wipers, 10 cat-cow flows

exercises.name: Reclined Twist (Supta Matsyendrasana)
exercises.notes: Lie supine, hug knee to chest, then gently guide it across your body. Keep shoulders planted on floor. This wrings out digestive organs, releases lower-back tension, and primes diaphragmatic breathing.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Rotational Twist
exercises.notes: Half-kneel with hips squared forward, place rear hand behind head, and rotate torso toward front leg. Keep core engaged to isolate thoracic rotation. This opens ribs, improves spinal mobility for daily movement, and strengthens obliques with zero impact.

exercises.name: Seated Forward Fold with Spinal Elongation (Paschimottanasana)
exercises.notes: Sit with legs extended, inhale to lengthen spine, exhale to fold. Avoid forcing hamstring depth; focus on neutral spine and breathing. This stretches the entire posterior chain and signals your body it's time to rest.

exercises.name: Supported Fish Pose (Matsyasana with block)
exercises.notes: Place a yoga block under your upper back, let shoulders relax back, and breathe into your chest. This gentle chest and shoulder opener counteracts rounded-shoulder posture from desk work and trains deep breathing capacity.

exercises.name: Extended Child's Pose (Balasana)
exercises.notes: Knees wide, big toes together, sink hips to heels, arms extended forward. Breathe into your back ribs. This deeply restful pose activates the vagus nerve and signals nervous system downregulation.

workout.cooldown: 5 min: supine spinal twist 1 min each side, reclined butterfly stretch 1 min, savasana with 3-part breath (inhale 4 counts, hold 4, exhale 4) for 2 min
workout.description: A 40-minute beginner-friendly recovery yoga session emphasizing gentle twists, spinal mobility, and diaphragmatic breathing to reduce muscular tension and activate the parasympathetic nervous system. Perfect for fat-loss athletes seeking active recovery that supports digestion and reduces cortisol while improving thoracic rotation and core resilience.

meal.title: Seared Duck Breast and Lentil-Free Warm Grain Bowl with Ginger Sesame Glaze
meal.description: Starting duck in a cold pan and slowly rendering the fat gives you crispy skin every time without burning. No special skills required.
meal.instructions:
Ingredients:
2 duck breasts (skin-on)
1 cup cooked farro or barley
1 cup baby spinach
1/2 cup shredded purple cabbage
1/2 cup edamame (shelled)
1 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce
1 tsp fresh grated ginger
1 tsp sesame oil
1 tbsp rice vinegar
1 tsp honey
1 tsp sesame seeds
Salt and black pepper

Instructions:
1. Score the duck skin in a crosshatch pattern, season with salt and pepper. Place skin-side down in a cold pan, then turn heat to medium. Cook for 8-10 minutes until the skin is golden and crisp, then flip and cook 4-5 more minutes. Rest for 5 minutes, then slice thin. 2. Whisk together soy sauce, ginger, sesame oil, rice vinegar, and honey to make the glaze. 3. Build bowls with farro, spinach, cabbage, and edamame. Lay sliced duck on top, drizzle glaze over everything. 4. Finish with sesame seeds.
